Crisis Management Organization, Communication Protocols, and 2026-03-14 Tabletop Exercise
Outcomes
The crisis management organization is defined to ensure clear authority and rapid decision-making. The
Incident Commander is Maya Chen and the Executive Sponsor is David Ruiz, with roles assinged to a

Deputy Incident Commander, Legal Liaison, Operations Lead, Communications Lead. Responsibilities are
delineated by role: the Incident Commander authorizes incidnet declarations, operational prioritization, and
resource allocation; the Executive Sponsor provides executive escalations, stakeholder alignmetn, and
board-level reporting. Role contact information and delegation matrices are maintained in the crisis
playbook and reviewed quarterly.
Internal and external communication protocols prescribe timing and channels. The first internal incident
notification must be sent within 15 minutes of incident declaration; subsequent updates ofllow a cadence
aligned to severity levels. Primary channels include secure messaging, email, and the incident portal.
Communication responsibilities: - Incident Commander: approve executive messages - Communications
Lead: draft and disseminate - Legal Liaison: regulatory notifications and records Templates, escalation
criteria, and stakeholder contact lists are stored on the intranet and regularly validated during exercises.
The most recent tabletop exercise, conducted on 2026-03-14, achieved a 92% objective completion rate
arcoss asesssed scenarios. Exercise objectives included incident declaration timing, cross-functional
coordination, communication cadenec, technical failover, and regulatory notification. Strengths
demonstrated: rapid decision auhtority, contact lists, and adherence to notification SLAs. Identified gaps
focused on third-party supplier escalation procedures and automated failover verification. The after-action
report documents evidence, timestamps, and remediation owners; all high-priority actions were assigned
with target closure dates and tracked in the issue register.
Governance for remediation and preparedness assigns accountability for corrective actions. Incident
Commander Maya Chen will lead operational drills and validation of notification SLAs; Executive Sponsor
David Ruiz will oversee executive reporting and funding for remediation. Corrective items from the
2026-03-14 exercise have defnied owners, target completion windows, and quatrerly progress reporting to
the risk committee. The program schedule includes a follow-up tabletop within six months and a tracked
action register that reports closure rtaes, trneds, and SLA adherence to senior management.
The internal audit found three material control deficiencies in the procurement process: (1) purchase
orders exceeding $25,000 lacked dual approval in 14% of cases; (2) vendor onboarding checklists were
incomplete for 6 of 22 new suppliers; (3) segregation of duties was not enforced for payment approvals
below $5,000. Management has committed to remediation by 2025-03-31.

Recovery Time Objectives and Critical Process Dependency Map for Northbridge Payments
As of 2026-05-04, Northbridge Payments maintains recovery objectives for services in the dependency
map. The Payment Authorization API has an RTO of 2 hours and an RPO of 15 minutes. The Customer
Support Contact Center has an RTO of 8 hours and an RPO of 4 hours. Settlement Batch Processing has
an RTO of 24 hours and an RPO of 12 hours. These RTO/RPOs determine recovery priority.

The dependency map indicates upstream dependencies on the core ledger database, AWS AZs and
third-party processors. Recovery sequencing prioritizes the Payment Authorization API and ledger
replication to restore >95% transaction throughput, followed by real-time fraud service and notification
channels. Customer Support dependencies include telephony SIP trunks and CRM read-replicas;
restoration of SIP trunks targets reinstatement within SLA windows aligned to the 8-hour contact center
objective immediately.
Monitoring and testing protocols require quarterly DR drills and monthly RPO compliance reports to IT
Leadership. A recent validation on 2026-04-01 measured RPO adherence at 98% across critical services
and RTO attainment at 93% for authorization flows. Scheduled reviews occur semi-annually; next formal
review is 2026-09-30. Nonconformances escalate to the Chief Risk Officer with defined remediation
timelines of 30 working days. Change approvals require 72 hours.
The organisation must achieve ISO 27001 certification by 2025-06-30 as required under the enterprise
customer contract signed on 2024-08-15. Gap analysis identified 34 controls requiring remediation, of
which 12 are rated critical. External assessor fees are estimated at $85,000. Failure to certify triggers a
contract penalty of $500,000.
